clue.text: King Edward, say, limited as art patron

indicators.note: limited means cut short, so the word loses its final letter here

parts.note: a King Edward is a British potato variety, and tater is slang for potato

explanation.surface: A remark that an English king was a restricted sort of patron of the arts.
explanation.walkthrough: King Edward is a well-known British potato variety, so it suggests TATER; 'limited' drops its last letter R.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Henry Tate, sugar magnate, founded the London gallery and is a celebrated benefactor of art.

clue.text: Set of characters concealing truth, mainly, in Melville novel

indicators.note: concealing means hiding something within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Typee is Herman Melville's first novel, set in the Marquesas

indicators.note: mainly means most of it, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a fact is a truth

explanation.surface: A Melville novel is said to have a cast of characters hiding the truth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set of characters' suggests a novel's cast, but it is printing type.
explanation.definitionFit: A typeface is a designed set of printed letters and symbols.

clue.text: Irritating as first part of 6 is out of order

indicators.note: out of order means the letters are not in their proper sequence and must be rearranged

parts.note: the first word of the answer to 6 down

explanation.surface: Something annoys because the first component of a device is broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of order' rearranges REMOTE (the first word of 6 down) with IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tiresome is wearisome and annoying, so irritating fits as an adjective.

clue.text: Show disapproval of stupid trick, in charge as work assessor

parts.note: to boo is to jeer in disapproval

indicators.note: stupid suggests the word trick is muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone jeers at a silly trick while the one in charge sits in judgement on the work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stupid' is the anagram signal; the surface makes it sound like a verdict on the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A reviewer of books assesses literary works, so 'work assessor' is a fair description.

clue.text: A stone circle erected, last in series

indicators.note: erected means set upright, so in a down entry the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a gem is a precious stone
O is shaped like a circle

explanation.surface: A ring of standing stones is put up, the final one in a sequence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erected' turns A, GEM and O upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the final letter of the Greek alphabet, hence the end of a series.

clue.text: Flirtatious as queen in her youth, perhaps

definitions.text: as queen in her youth, perhaps
definitions.meaning: a queen is a female cat, so a young one behaves like a kitten

explanation.walkthrough: 'queen' looks royal but is a female cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A coquettish person is playful like a young cat, and a young queen cat is literally a kitten.

clue.text: It can change the views of those who aren't watching closely

definitions.text: It can change the views of those who aren't watching closely

parts.words: It can change the views of those who aren't watching closely
parts.note: a handheld device switching TV channels for viewers sitting at a distance, not close to the set

explanation.definitionFit: The handset switches channels from across the room, so viewers far from the screen change what they see.

clue.text: Speculation of political type he's entertained

indicators.note: entertained means taken in as a guest, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: a Tory is a British Conservative
he, the 's meaning is and serving as a link

explanation.surface: A politician of a certain party is hosting a man who speculates.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory is a conjecture or hypothesis, a speculation.

clue.text: Stick to colour of cold fabric

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
rayon is a synthetic fabric

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep to the shade of a chilly cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick to' reads as a verb phrase, but it is a noun: a stick for colouring.
explanation.definitionFit: A crayon is a stick of wax or chalk used for colouring.

clue.text: Meat product nobody should buy

definitions.meaning: a British pastry case filled with chopped pork
to buy is to believe, and a porky (rhyming slang from the pastry) is a lie nobody should swallow

explanation.definitionFit: The pastry is a British snack, and its rhyming-slang sense means a lie, something no one should believe.

clue.text: Rich with playrooms, perhaps, a first-class establishment?

indicators.note: perhaps hints the letters could be arranged differently

explanation.surface: A wealthy place with playrooms might be a top-rate school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges RICH and PLAYROOMS. 'first-class' suggests excellence, but here it is the first stage of school.
explanation.definitionFit: A school for the earliest years of education is literally an establishment for the first classes.

clue.text: Cause of road rage when followed by a vehicle

indicators.note: says the next piece comes straight after the first one

parts.note: losing one's temper is what drives road rage

explanation.surface: A motorist's fury is sparked when another car tailgates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vehicle' looks like a car, but in painting a vehicle is the medium that carries pigment.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempera is a painting medium, and in art a vehicle is the liquid binder carrying the pigment.

clue.text: Devious fiancé's seizing a time to use charm

indicators.note: seizing means grabbing hold of, so one piece is clasped inside the other
devious means winding or crooked, so the letters of the word are twisted round

explanation.surface: A scheming husband-to-be grabs his chance to win someone over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Devious' shuffles FIANCES into FASCINE, and 'seizing' puts A and T inside it. The 's counts as a letter here.
explanation.definitionFit: To charm someone is to captivate them, the same as to fascinate.

clue.text: Piece of bronze that's a ton, approximately

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for ton
or so means roughly, about

explanation.surface: A bronze sculpture is said to weigh about a ton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece of bronze' means a sculpture, not a fragment of metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A torso is a common subject for a bronze sculpture, the trunk without head or limbs.

clue.text: Records agreement to hold talks without us

parts.note: a compact is a formal agreement or pact

indicators.note: without signals that the following letters are dropped

parts.note: to discuss is to hold talks about something

explanation.surface: A deal is struck to hold negotiations from which we are excluded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to hold' looks like a container signal, but it belongs with 'talks'; 'without' does the removing.
explanation.definitionFit: Compact discs are recordings of music, so records in the plural fits.

clue.text: Small plane, say, as possible transport for newly-weds in air

definitions.meaning: a light aircraft carrying a pilot and one passenger

definitions.text: possible transport for newly-weds in air
definitions.meaning: an aircraft just big enough for a couple flying off together

explanation.definitionFit: A light aircraft with room for two suits a married couple flying off alone.

clue.text: Aggressive pressmen following British group of young celebrities

indicators.note: following means the next piece comes after the first

parts.note: the rat pack is a pushy mob of journalists and photographers

explanation.surface: Pushy journalists trail a British set of young stars.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a clique of young famous actors or performers, originally Hollywood stars of the 1980s.

clue.text: Religious music with European score and French composer

parts.note: a mass is a musical setting of the Eucharist
to net is to score a goal

explanation.surface: Church music combined with a European score comes from a French composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'score' suggests a musical score but means to net a goal.
explanation.definitionFit: Jules Massenet was a French opera composer, known for Manon.

clue.text: Cause of ill-feeling one may well experience

definitions.text: Cause of ill-feeling one may well experience

parts.words: Cause of ill-feeling one may well experience

clue.text: Asians with faith in British industry

indicators.note: in signals the answer sits inside the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: Asian believers are working in British industry.
explanation.definitionFit: Hindus are followers of Hinduism, chiefly from South Asia.

clue.text: Old man covering an object of worship in temple

indicators.note: covering means wrapping round, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father
an gives the letter A
a god is an object of worship

explanation.surface: A father protects a sacred idol inside a temple.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagoda is a tiered tower temple in East Asia.

clue.text: Patriarch is a leader of ancient clan, originally

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
originally points to the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A tribal patriarch is described as the founding head of an old clan.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac, son of Abraham and father of Jacob, is one of the biblical patriarchs.

clue.text: Organise, with haste, pure running water in Iraq

indicators.note: organise tells us to arrange the letters of the words in a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to quickly set up a supply of clean flowing water in Iraq.
explanation.definitionFit: The Euphrates is a great river flowing through Iraq.

clue.text: Steps deliberately executed, parking a vehicle

parts.note: P is the sign for parking
a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Careful steps are taken while parking a van.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steps deliberately executed' means slow dance steps, not a manoeuvre.
explanation.definitionFit: The pavane is a stately, slow processional court dance, so steps performed with deliberation.

clue.text: Make fresh start at Rugby as withdrawn student

definitions.meaning: in rugby, a kick from the 22-metre line restarting play
someone who abandons a course of study

explanation.walkthrough: Rugby looks like the English school, which suits the student, but it is the game.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby union the term names a restarting kick, and it also means someone leaving their studies.

clue.text: One played badly in football team at home

parts.note: Villa is short for Aston Villa, an English football club
in means at home

explanation.surface: A player performs poorly for a football side in a home match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'played badly' suggests poor football; it means a part acted as a bad person. ASTON VILLA is a Birmingham football club.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor plays the villain, the bad character, so it is a role played as wicked.

clue.text: Inconspicuous part of agreement that makes little impression

parts.note: little means small
a print is an impression made on a surface

explanation.surface: A hidden clause in a contract barely registers with the reader.
explanation.definitionFit: The fine terms in a contract printed in tiny type are easy to overlook.

clue.text: Took place at table holding king in card game

indicators.note: holding means one piece encloses another

parts.note: to take one's place at table is to sit, past tense sat
K is the abbreviation for king in cards and chess

explanation.surface: A player sat down at the table holding a king during a game of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Skat is a German three-player card game.
